qa_pairs.question: In 2023, does the proportion distribution trend of the main offline night - time shopping channels (malls and supermarkets, convenience stores) among Chinese residents match the proportion distribution trend of the main types of offline night - time entertainment activities (watching movies in the cinema, exercising and fitness)? Answer yes or no.
qa_pairs.explanation: In offline night - time shopping, malls and supermarkets (65.8%) and convenience stores (55.0%) both have relatively high proportions, showing a trend of multi - channel activity. In offline night - time entertainment activities, watching movies in the cinema (51.91%) and exercising and fitness (45.53%) also have relatively high proportions, showing a trend of multi - type activity. The distribution trends of the two are consistent.

qa_pairs.question: In 2023, is there an obvious correlation between the proportion of live - streaming/short - video shopping in online night - time shopping among Chinese residents (15.2% + 10.3%) and the proportion of watching short videos/live - streams in online night - time entertainment (59.0% + 42.3%)? Answer yes or no.
qa_pairs.explanation: Live - streaming and short - videos are not only the main activities in online entertainment (with a combined proportion of 101.3%), but also important channels for online shopping (with a combined proportion of 25.5%). They belong to the same live - streaming/short - video ecosystem, and there is a possibility of scenario linkage, so there is a certain correlation.

qa_pairs.question: In 2023, is there an extreme - value correspondence among the night - time catering consumption method with the highest proportion (dine - in at the restaurant, 32.5%), the offline night - time shopping channel with the highest proportion (malls and supermarkets, 65.8%), and the offline night - time entertainment activity with the highest proportion (watching movies in the cinema, 51.91%) among Chinese residents? Answer yes or no.
qa_pairs.explanation: Dine - in at the restaurant, shopping in malls and supermarkets, and watching movies in the cinema all belong to offline physical consumption scenarios, and they are all the options with the highest proportions in their respective fields. There is a certain behavioral linkage correspondence in the common scenario of 'offline night - time physical consumption'.

qa_pairs.question: Among consumers who mainly dine - in at restaurants at night, what percentage also prefer to watch movies in the cinema? Round to 1 decimal place. Answer: xx.x%
qa_pairs.explanation: Dine - in at the restaurant accounts for 32.5% of night - time catering consumption, and watching movies in the cinema accounts for 51.91% of offline entertainment. Multiplying the two gives 32.5%×51.91% = 16.87%. Rounding to 1 decimal place is 16.9%.

qa_pairs.question: What is the multiple relationship between the preference for online food delivery consumption and the preference for online shopping on e - commerce platforms at night? Round to 2 decimal places. Answer: xx.xx times
qa_pairs.explanation: Dividing the preference for online shopping on e - commerce platforms (69.4%) by the preference for online food delivery consumption (23.3%) gives 69.4%÷23.3%≈2.97854. Rounding to 2 decimal places is 2.98 times.

qa_pairs.question: In the preference for offline shopping channels, by how many percentage points does the preference for malls and supermarkets exceed the preference for 'gathering with friends' entertainment offline? Round to 1 decimal place. Answer: xx.x%
qa_pairs.explanation: Subtracting the preference for gathering with friends offline (40.99%) from the preference for malls and supermarkets offline (65.8%) gives 65.8%−40.99% = 24.81%. Rounding to 1 decimal place is 24.8%.

answer.B: Increase the supply of night-time goods and experiential services in offline hotspots such as convenience stores and pedestrian streets. answer.C: Reduce the prices of all goods to attract more consumers, as price sensitivity is a key factor affecting purchase decisions.
answer.D: Increase night-time advertising investment to enhance brand awareness, which can indirectly stimulate consumer demand.
